text:
sara_sales: Quick heads-up — FinPay wants a Dedicated POC. They need the dedicated endpoint locked down to an allowlist of customer IPs and want confirmation about how stable egress IPs are for the life of the POC. Also asking whether we can do cert-based auth or only API-key scoping. Need an answer for the security questionnaire by EOD.

mike_netops: We can provision static egress IPs for a dedicated pool. For a POC we usually reserve 2 static IPs from our EIP pool. They remain stable unless we reprovision/rotate the pool. Note: mutual TLS termination is supported on Private deployments; hosted/dedicated endpoints currently support API-key + IP allowlist, not mTLS on our edge.

alex_engineer: Quick technical confirm: dedicated pools support per-customer source-IP allowlist. Rotation only occurs on reprovisioning. I'll prepare the curl test and firewall snippet. Example quick test:

```
curl -X POST
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <DEDI_KEY>'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  https://dedicated-us-west.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```

leah_se: Customer also asked whether model instances can make outbound calls to external APIs (they want webhooks). Do outbound egress flows from the pool use the same NAT IPs?

mike_netops: Yes — outbound from instances to external services goes out via the same NAT/EIP addresses. So if they need to whitelist us to receive callbacks at their infra, they should allow the dedicated pool IPs. If they can't open firewall rules, recommend webhook relay or have the customer proxy outbound traffic through their NAT. We can also set up a temporary jump host for deeper debugging.

sara_sales: Can you confirm we can commit to keeping the IPs static for a 30-day POC? Also need a one-line answer I can paste into the security questionnaire about allowlisting.

alex_engineer: One-liner you can use: "Yes — Dedicated endpoint pools support customer IP allowlisting; we can provision static egress IPs for the duration of the POC and document any rotations required."

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Dedicated pool request (poc-finpay-2026) submitted by @sara_sales. Provisioning started. Step status: 1/3 resources created. ETA ~2h.

mike_netops: :thumbsup: I'll follow up after provisioning completes. Sara — please send the customer CIDRs and point-of-contact for their network team. If they require mTLS we'll need to move to Private and open a separate design thread.

sara_sales: Got CIDRs from Claire: 203.0.113.45/32 and 198.51.100.0/24. They prefer no mTLS for the POC. I'm sharing Claire (Claire.N@finpay.example) for network coordination.

alex_engineer: Thanks — once pool is live I'll post the allocated egress IPs and the exact firewall rules to add. I'll also include the example curl above and note that the dedicated API key is scoped to the pool and can be revoked anytime.

mike_netops: Reminder: keys are scoped to the pool. For customers wanting cert-auth we support full mTLS in Private deployments, but for this POC we'll proceed with IP allowlist + dedicated key.

sara_sales: Perfect — I'll update the security questionnaire with Alex's line and confirm the 30-day timeline with FinPay.

leah_se: Checklist: CIDRs received, pool provisioning in progress, will publish egress IPs + firewall snippet when ready. :white_check_mark:
